# A lifetime in a non-reactive loop is refused, and the reactive one still builds.
#
# A `for` holds many copies of its body whether or not it is reactive, and only a
# *reactive* one elects a runtime instance -- which is what gives each copy state
# of its own. Over a `const` iterable nothing can change, so the body is spliced
# once and its vars hoisted once: every pass shares the one handle, the second
# mount overwrites the first, and the schedule the first opened runs on with
# nothing able to stop it.
#
# Shared state is the documented cost of a non-reactive loop for an ordinary
# component. For a lifetime it is a leak, so it is refused rather than paid.
# #245 is the real fix -- route a stateful component to a runtime instance
# whether or not the position is reactive -- and until that lands this is the
# loud half of what main did by accident, which was to fail with "fyne primitive
# Timer was instantiated without a spec record".
#
# A txtar rather than a testdata fixture: the refusal is passNoInlineComponents',
# and ERROR(lower) is a phase nothing evaluates -- only parse, check and test
# are. A fixture written that way asserts nothing at all.

! sngl generate --platform fyne --lang go -o out constloop.sngl
stderr 'brackets a lifetime and this loop is not reactive'
stderr 'see #245'
! stderr 'panic'

# A reactive `if` inside the same const loop is the same defect by another
# route: it sets the "needs reconciling" bit, which elects a runtime instance --
# but the loop var is still one hoisted cell, and the emitted Go did not even
# compile (`undefined: p`). What decides per-copy state is the *loop*, so that
# is the bit the refusal reads.
! sngl generate --platform fyne --lang go -o out constloopif.sngl
stderr 'brackets a lifetime and this loop is not reactive'

# One word is the whole difference, and the other word still works.
sngl generate --platform fyne --lang go -o out varloop.sngl
grep 'TimerInstance' out/model.go

# The boundary, which matters more than the message. A loop over the same const
# list builds when what it holds brackets no lifetime...
sngl generate --platform fyne --lang go -o out stateless.sngl

# ...and so does a component with state of its own, which shares a cell here and
# always has. Widening the refusal to that would refuse programs that work.
sngl generate --platform fyne --lang go -o out stateful.sngl

# And a lifetime outside any loop is untouched.
sngl generate --platform fyne --lang go -o out plain.sngl
grep 'NewTicker' out/model.go

-- constloop.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

var n = 0
const periods list<time.duration> = [100ms, 250ms]

ui.window(title="t") {
    for var p = periods {
        time.timer(interval=p, enabled=true, @tick { n = n + 1 })
    }
    ui.text(value=string(n))
}
-- constloopif.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

var n = 0
const periods list<time.duration> = [100ms, 250ms]

ui.window(title="t") {
    for var p = periods {
        if n < 100 {
            time.timer(interval=p, enabled=true, @tick { n = n + 1 })
        }
    }
}
-- varloop.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

var n = 0
var periods list<time.duration> = [100ms, 250ms]

ui.window(title="t") {
    for var p = periods {
        time.timer(interval=p, enabled=true, @tick { n = n + 1 })
    }
    ui.text(value=string(n))
}
-- stateless.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

const labels list<string> = ["a", "b"]

ui.window(title="t") {
    for var l = labels {
        ui.text(value=l)
    }
}
-- stateful.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

const labels list<string> = ["a", "b"]

component counter(label = "") ui.node {
    var hits = 0
    ui.button(text="{label} {hits}", @click { hits = hits + 1 })
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    for var l = labels {
        counter(label=l)
    }
}
-- plain.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

var n = 0

ui.window(title="t") {
    time.timer(interval=100ms, enabled=true, @tick { n = n + 1 })
    ui.text(value=string(n))
}
